newsitem.title: UK: Rugby to sell metal units for 33.2 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Rugby to sell metal units for 33.2 mln stg.

text.p: Construction materials firm Rugby Group Plc said on Thursday that it had agreed to sell its metal buildings unit Ward Buildings Systems Ltd and ZND Bouwstaal BV for a total consideration of 33.2 million stg.
Rugby said it was selling Ward for 25.9 million stg.
The company would, however, retain title to debtors, creditors and work-in-progress of Ward's strucutures division, which are expected to realise an additional five million stg.
Ward comrpises three trading divisions -- components, structures, and Atlas (UK) -- employing 637 people.
Ward's net operating assets totalled 17.5 million stg as on December 31, 1995.
The unit had reported operating profits of 1.6 million stg on sales of 45.1 million stg for the six months to June, 1996.
ZND manufactures a range of steel wire and bar products including security fencing and concrete reinforcements from its factory in south east Netherlands, where it employs 75 people.
Rugby is selling this unit for 2.3 million stg, to its management team.
The transaction involves an estimated loss of 4.9 million stg for Rugby.
Peter Johnson, chief executive of Rugby, said: "Their sale would enable us to focus on the development of our international cement lime and joinery operations".
